title: credential-broker.v1
description: The Connections credential broker's wire: the signed caller assertion every request carries, and the request and response bodies of each route. Callers are agent-api (role agent, and role git for the Git credential store) and the terminal's server routes (role human). An agent-role or git-role call also carries the gateway's X-Vexa-Identity (gateway-identity.v1) for the person it acts for, and its subject must be the assertion's actor. The broker never returns a stored credential to the agent or human roles; only the git role reads a value back, for Git operations agent-api performs itself. Status codes: 401 a missing or bad assertion or signed identity; 403 a role or name this caller may not use; 409 a refusal the person can act on (reconnect, grant, fix the setup); 422 a body that does not validate; 502 an upstream that answered unusably; 503 an upstream that cannot be reached or is rate-limiting. Every non-2xx body is an Error.

MailCredentialRequest.description: flows, the deployment's one mail sender, asks for the outbound relay's password the install names by reference (`VEXA_MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD_REF=broker:mail/<name>`, PRD 0.13.4 S2). Only `service/mail/<name>` is reachable, and only with the flows broker key (the sensors role); the operator stores the value with `python -m credential_broker.mail_secret put <name>` (value on stdin).

value.description: the relay password; flows keeps it in memory only and never logs it

SignalsModelKeyRequest.description: the signals service asks for the signal model's key the company policy names (`model_signals.secret_ref: broker:signals/<name>`). Only `service/signals/<name>` is reachable, and only by the signals role; the operator stores the value with `python -m credential_broker.signals_key put <name>` (value on stdin).

value.description: the model key; the signals service keeps it in memory only and never logs it

CalendarChangesRequest.description: flows' calendar sensor asks what changed on the person's connected Google Calendar since `cursor` (the provider's sync token, opaque). No cursor: a bounded first read (one day back to sixty days ahead) that returns the first cursor. The broker holds the token, makes the call and returns events, never a credential. It reads only under a live SensorGrant the owner issued on the connection read; without one the answer is 409 with reason `sensor_grant_required` (none, revoked or expired).

owner.description: the person whose connection is read; must equal the assertion's actor

connection_id.description: one of the owner's ready google_calendar connections; omitted = the one with the owner's newest live sensor grant, else their most recent one

cursor.description: the next sync token; null with resync_required

resync_required.description: the cursor went stale (the provider answered 410): drop it and read again without one

SensorGrantRequest.description: The person lets flows' sensors read one ready google_calendar connection of theirs (scope `calendar.read`) for `days`. Only the agent role (the gateway's X-Vexa-Identity for the person, in a watched turn no one else reads) and the human role (the terminal, for the signed-in person) may issue one; never the sensors role. A new grant revokes the live one on the same connection.

connection_id.description: omitted = the person's most recent ready google_calendar connection

SensorGrant.description: One sensor grant: whose (the caller), which connection, what (`calendar.read`), until when. `issued_via` is `person`, or `upgrade` for a grant adopted once at upgrade (30 days) on a calendar the broker's own audit shows a sensor read successfully in the 14 days before.

CalendarChange.description: one changed calendar event, normalised; untrusted content (titles are written by whoever sent the invite)

start.description: ISO-8601 with offset, or a date for an all-day event

video_url.description: the meeting link: Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Jitsi, https only

Role.description: agent: agent-api acting for the person in the forwarded X-Vexa-Identity — may request, prepare, list and USE connections, never consent or store a credential. human: the terminal's server routes for a signed-in person — may also consent, store, disconnect and delete. git: agent-api's Git credential store, for the person in the forwarded X-Vexa-Identity — may only read and write that person's Git credentials (pat/<person>, deploy/user-<person>.*) and the deploy keys of the shared workspaces among the memberships signed with them (deploy/ws-<id>.*). bots: meeting-api's bot-account store (ADR-0049) — may only list, read, save, re-state and delete saved signed-in browser profiles; it carries no X-Vexa-Identity (meeting-api acts for a bot), and its actor is `user:<id>`, `company` or `meeting-api`. sensors: flows' sensor pool (ADR-0050) — may only read a person's connected calendar's CHANGES since a cursor (`/api/internal/sensor/calendar-changes`, read-only, results never a credential), and only under a live sensor grant that person issued on that connection (`/api/sensor-grants`, agent or human role; the sensors role cannot issue one); it carries no X-Vexa-Identity (a sensor runs with nobody in the loop) and its actor is the person (`<uid>`) whose connection is read; the same flows key also reads the outbound relay's password the install names (`/api/internal/mail/smtp-credential`, `service/mail/<name>` only, actor `flows-mail`). signals: the transcript-signals service — may only read the signal model's key the company policy names (`/api/internal/signals/model-key`, `service/signals/<name>` only); it carries no X-Vexa-Identity (no person is in the loop) and its actor is `signals`.

Assertion.description: The claims carried in the X-Vexa-Assertion header as base64url(JSON), unpadded, followed by '.' and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of that encoded part under the role's key. Accepted from 30 seconds before to 5 seconds after the broker's clock, once (nonce), and only for the exact method, path with query, and body bytes it names.

actor.description: The subject the request acts for. Connections are owned by, and filtered on, this value.

session.description: human: a keyed digest of the browser's sign-in cookie, which binds an OAuth callback to the session that started it. agent and git: a per-request correlation id.

at.description: Unix seconds when the assertion was signed.

nonce.description: Single-use; the broker refuses a second request carrying it.

path.description: The exact request path, plus '?' and the raw query when there is one.

body.description: SHA-256 of the exact request body bytes, hex (the empty body hashes to e3b0c442…).

SignedAssertionVector.description: A deterministic interop vector: both language bindings must produce exactly `encoded`, `signature` and `header` from `key` and `claims`, and must verify `header` for the bound request. The key is a published test value, never a deployment key.

request_body.description: The exact body bytes, as UTF-8 text, whose SHA-256 is claims.body.

Provider.description: google_email and google_calendar use Google OAuth with fixed scopes. custom_secret stores any secret and, optionally, uses it at one human-approved HTTPS endpoint.

SetupSpec.description: A declarative setup a caller proposes. It takes effect only when a human saves the credential for it; the destination host is shown to that human and must be confirmed on first save.

prefix.description: scheme=prefix only: the one-token word sent before the credential (`Authorization: <prefix> <credential>`), e.g. Bot or Token

setup_request.description: Changes whenever a caller asks for this connection's setup again; the panel opens on a change.

account.description: The provider account address when the provider reports one (Gmail).

setup.description: The prepared SetupSpec, or {} when none was prepared.

approved_host.description: The destination hosts a human last approved for this connection's credentials, space-separated (for OAuth the token-exchange host and the service endpoint host); a prepared setup naming any other host must be confirmed again (M3).

permissions.description: The optional permissions the stored grant carries: drafts (Gmail compose), calendar_write (Google calendar.events).

setup_request.description: The setup_request the human reviewed; a stale value is refused so a re-prepared setup cannot ride an older approval.

confirmed_host.description: Required on the first save of a prepared setup: the destination host the human typed to confirm where the secret will be sent.
Required on the first save: the token-exchange host, which receives the client secret.

confirmed_hosts.description: The other hosts the person typed: required on the first save to a service endpoint host that is not the token-exchange host, because it receives the person's access token on every call.

AccountReadResponse.description: Provider content projected to a fixed field set. untrusted_content is always true: mail and calendar text is third-party input to the agent. Every Gmail message may carry web_url (GmailWebUrl) and every Calendar event web_url (CalendarWebUrl): the only link to a message or event an agent may give a person. Optional, added in 2026-10; older readers ignore it.

drafts.description: gmail.thread only: the drafts among the returned messages, each with its draft id. Optional, added in 2026-10.

request_id.description: Idempotency key: a retry with the same id and identical content returns the first result.

thread_id.description: Reply in this thread (from a Gmail read): In-Reply-To, References and the Re: subject are set by the broker.

in_reply_to.description: The Gmail message id replied to; empty = the thread's last message.

Error.description: Every non-2xx answer. detail is a fixed sentence; it never echoes input, a credential or a provider response body. 409 is a refusal the person can act on; 502 and 503 are faults to retry later, never a request to reconnect. reason, when present, is what a caller acts on.

reason.description: store_unavailable: the credential store does not answer or refuses the broker (503) — an outage, reconnecting cannot help. reconnect_required: the provider no longer accepts the stored authorization or a permission is missing (409) — the person reconnects. provider_error: the provider or service refused for another reason (409) or is down (502/503) — reconnecting does not help. sensor_grant_required: a sensor read for a person with no live sensor grant on that calendar — none, revoked or expired (409); the person grants it, reconnecting does not help.

store.description: Which credential store backend this broker writes to.

Readiness.description: GET /ready, the readiness probe: 200 with status ok while the credential store answers, 503 with status unavailable while it does not. GET /health is liveness and stays ok while the store is down.

GmailWebUrl.description: Built by the broker, never taken from the caller or the provider: Gmail's web address of the thread (the message id only when Gmail gave no thread id) in the CONNECTED mailbox, https://mail.google.com/mail/?authuser=<connected address, percent-encoded>#all/<thread id>. The address is the one the broker recorded at consent and selects the signed-in browser session with Google's authuser parameter; the link never names an account index (/u/0/) and never the path /mail/u/<address>/, which Gmail answers with its own Temporary Error (404) page. Absent when the broker holds no address for the connection.

CalendarWebUrl.description: The event's Google htmlLink, passed through only when it is an https URL on calendar.google.com or www.google.com with no port or user info; absent otherwise.

AccountReadMessage.description: One Gmail message projected to a fixed field set. Fields beyond those listed are reserved for future optional additions.

labels.description: Gmail's labelIds for the message (DRAFT, SENT, INBOX, user label ids). Optional, added in 2026-10.

is_draft.description: True when the message is an unsent draft (its labels carry DRAFT): it has not been sent. Optional, added in 2026-10.

draft_id.description: gmail.thread only: the draft id of a draft message, for a draft update. Optional, added in 2026-10.

AccountReadEvent.description: One Calendar event projected to a fixed field set (htmlLink is kept as Google sent it; web_url is the vetted copy).

ActionPolicy.description: The administrator's connection policy (`_global/POLICIES.md`), narrowed by the person, as agent-api resolved it for this action. The broker enforces it again. Absent: no background use, no attendee mail, the primary calendar only, no attachments. A null list means any.

unattended.description: connection_actions_unattended allows this action for a worker without a person in the loop.

ActionPreferences.description: A person's own narrower setting for the connection policy keys; an absent key means as the administrator allows. agent-api refuses a setting wider than the administrator's policy.

AuthorizeRequest.description: Optional. `grant` asks for an additional permission on top of the connection's base scopes (incremental consent).

request_id.description: Idempotency key: a retry with the same id and identical content returns the first result.

thread_id.description: Reply in this thread (from a Gmail read): In-Reply-To, References and the Re: subject are set by the broker.

in_reply_to.description: The Gmail message id replied to; empty = the thread's last message.

draft_id.description: A draft id this broker created for this person (from a GmailDraftResponse), or with replace_person_draft a draft in this mailbox (from a gmail.thread read).

replace_person_draft.description: The person asked, in their own attended session, to replace a draft Vexa did not create. Without it such a draft id is refused (409); a shared session or one without a person in the loop is refused regardless (403). Optional, added in 2026-10.

GmailDraftUpdateRequest.description: Replace the content of a draft this broker created for this person; any other draft id is refused unless replace_person_draft is true.

CalendarTime.description: A timed instant (date_time, ISO 8601; time_zone required when it has no offset) or an all-day date.

request_id.description: Idempotency key: a retry with the same id and identical content returns the first result.

event_id.description: update and cancel: an event id from a calendar read; create: empty.

notify.description: Ask Google to email attendees; refused unless calendar_notify_attendees allows it.

BotAccountOwner.description: Who a bot account belongs to: one person (`user:<id>`) or the whole deployment (`company`).

BotAccountPlatform.description: The sign-in a bot account holds: google (Google Meet), microsoft (Teams), zoom.

BotAccountFile.description: One file of a session-profile.v1 browser profile, its bytes base64.

path.description: Relative to the profile directory; never absolute, never a `..` segment.

BotAccountRequest.description: meeting-api's bot-account store. list: the accounts whose owner is among `owners` (metadata only). get: one account and its profile files (404 when absent). put: create the account `id`, or replace its profile (owner and platform must match the stored ones, else 409); state becomes ok and verified_at now. state: set the account's state (verified_at now when ok). delete: destroy every stored version and the index entry (idempotent).

BotAccount.description: A bot account's metadata: never its profile files.

BotAccountResponse.description: `accounts`: the listed accounts, or the one account acted on (empty when delete found nothing). `files`: the profile, only for get; null otherwise.
